anomalies.observed: D31 is listed as a two-pin LED_GREEN part (Device LED, LED_0805 footprint), but the netlist connects D31 to four pins/nets: pin 1 to VOUTP, pin 2 to VOUTN, pin 3 to NET0162, and pin 4 to NET0183. This is the same four-pin bridge-rectifier topology used by D49.
anomalies.expected: A two-pin LED should only have pins 1 and 2 and should not occupy a four-pin bridge position. The D31 location should be a four-pin bridge rectifier (such as ABS2, like D49), or D31 should be removed if it is truly an LED.
anomalies.impact: If D31 is assembled as an LED, the four-pin bridge path cannot be implemented and the transformer center-tap/VOUTP/VOUTN circuit is open or misconnected. If the nets are forced together, an LED may short or bias VOUTP/VOUTN. In either case the board will not behave as the intended four-pin bridge/transformer common-mode path.

parsed.summary: The design files contain a clear component-type anomaly: D31 is specified as a two-pin LED but is connected as a four-pin bridge rectifier, unlike the correct D49 ABS2 bridge. This would change the Ethernet/transformer power or common-mode path and is the main deviation from the intended design.
